recognize_zh: 多顆大型母細胞，核圓至不規則、染色質細緻並有明顯核仁，胞質中等量淡藍；同視野有一顆分葉成熟嗜中性球，提示有顆粒球成熟，符合 AML 伴成熟（M2）。
features: Large blasts with moderate N:C ratio and moderate pale blue cytoplasm
Round to irregular or indented nuclei with fine chromatin
One to two prominent nucleoli in several blasts
Rare fine cytoplasmic granules; no definite Auer rods in this field
Accompanying mature segmented neutrophil indicating residual granulocytic maturation
describe_en: Aspirate smear shows a hemodilute field containing several large blasts. The blasts have round to indented nuclei with finely dispersed chromatin and prominent nucleoli, and a moderate rim of pale basophilic cytoplasm with occasional fine granules. A mature segmented neutrophil is present nearby, and no definite Auer rods are seen. Findings are consistent with myeloblasts; AML with maturation is supported by the presence of maturing granulocytes, but confirmation requires a full differential count, cytochemistry or flow cytometry, and genetic studies.

ddx.vs: Monoblasts have more abundant grey-blue vacuolated cytoplasm and delicately folded nuclei, with nonspecific esterase positivity and CD14/CD64 on flow cytometry.
Lymphoblasts are usually smaller with scant cytoplasm and are MPO negative with a B- or T-lymphoid immunophenotype.
This genetic subtype commonly shows AML-M2 morphology with salmon-pink granules, a single long Auer rod and perinuclear hofs, requiring cytogenetics or molecular testing to confirm.
Regenerating marrow shows a spectrum of granulated promyelocytes with perinuclear hofs and orderly maturation rather than agranular blasts with prominent nucleoli.
